6.1.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.1.text: The Bhagavad said, "He who performs his bounden action without depending on its fruit is the man of renunciation and the man of Yoga, not he who simply remains without his fires and actions."

6.1.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.1.text: The Lord said, "He who performs works that ought to be done without seeking their fruits—he is a sannyasin and yogin, and not he who maintains no sacred fires and performs no actions."

6.1.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.1.text: The Blessed Lord said, "He who performs an action which is his duty, without depending on the result of the action, is a monk and a yogi; not so in he who does not keep afire and is actionless."

6.1.author: Swami Sivananda
6.1.text: The Blessed Lord said: He who performs his bounden duty without depending on the fruits of his actions—he is a sannyasi and a yogi, not he who is without fire and without action.

6.1.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.1.text: Lord Shri Krishna said: He who acts out of duty, without considering the consequences, is truly spiritual and a true ascetic; not he who merely observes rituals or shuns all action.

6.2.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.2.text: What the learned call renunciation, O son of Pandu, know that to be the same as the Yoga. For, without renouncing intention for fruit, one does not become a man of Yoga.

6.2.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.2.text: That which is called Sannyasa (Jnana Yoga), know that to be Yoga (Karma Yoga), O Arjuna. For no one, among Karma Yogins, whose delusive identification of the body with the self has not been abandoned, becomes a true Karma Yogin.

6.2.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.2.text: That which they call monasticism, know that to be Yoga, O Pandava, for nobody who has not given up expectations can be a yogi.

6.2.author: Swami Sivananda
6.2.text: Do you, O Arjuna, know that Yoga is what they call renunciation; no one indeed becomes a Yogi who has not renounced their thoughts.

6.2.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.2.text: O Arjuna, renunciation is indeed what is known as right action. No one can become spiritually enlightened who has not renounced all desires.

6.3.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.3.text: For a sage, who is desirous of mounting upon the Yoga, action is said to be the cause; for the same sage, when he has mounted upon the Yoga, stillness is said to be the cause.

6.3.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.3.text: Action is said to be the means for the sage who seeks to climb the heights of Yoga; but when he has climbed the heights of Yoga, tranquility is said to be the means.

6.3.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.3.text: For the sage who wishes to ascend to (Dhyana-) yoga, action is said to be the means. For that person, once he has ascended to (Dhyana-)yoga, inaction alone is said to be the means.

6.3.author: Swami Sivananda
6.3.text: For a sage who wishes to attain to Yoga, action is said to be the means; for the same sage who has attained Yoga, inaction is said to be the means.

6.3.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.3.text: For the sage who seeks the heights of spiritual meditation, practice is the only method, and when they have attained it, they must maintain themselves there through continual self-control.

6.4.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.4.text: When a person indulges neither in what is desired by the senses nor in the actions for it, then, being a man who has renounced all intentions, he is said to have mounted on the path of Yoga.

6.4.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.4.text: For, when one loses attachment to the things of the senses and to actions, then they have abandoned all desires and are said to have climbed the heights of Yoga.

6.4.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.4.text: Verily, when a man who has given up thought about everything does not get attached to sense-objects or actions, he is then said to be established in Yoga.

6.4.author: Swami Sivananda
6.4.text: When a person is not attached to the sense-objects or to actions, having renounced all thoughts, then they are said to have attained Yoga.

6.4.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.4.text: When a man renounces even the thought of initiating action, and is not interested in sense objects or any results that may flow from his acts, then he truly understands spirituality.

6.5.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.5.text: Let a person lift themselves by themselves and let them not depress themselves. For, the self alone is the friend of the self and the self alone is the foe of the self.

6.5.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.5.text: One should raise oneself by one's own mind and not allow oneself to sink; for the mind alone is the friend of the self, and the mind alone is the foe of the self.

6.5.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.5.text: One should save oneself by oneself; one should not degrade oneself. For oneself is indeed one's own friend; oneself is indeed one's own enemy.

6.5.author: Swami Sivananda
6.5.text: One should raise oneself by one's own self alone; let not one lower oneself; for the self alone is one's own friend, and the self alone is one's own enemy.

6.5.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.5.text: Let him seek liberation with the help of his Highest Self, and never disgrace his own Self. For that Self is his only friend; yet it can also be his enemy.

6.6.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.6.text: The Self is the friend of that Self by which the Self has been verily subdued; but in the case of a person with an unsubdued Self, the Self alone would abide in enmity like an enemy.

6.6.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.6.text: The mind is the friend of him by whom it has been conquered. But for him whose mind is not conquered, the mind, like an enemy, remains hostile.

6.6.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.6.text: He who has conquered his own self by the self, his self is his own friend. But for one who has not conquered his own self, his self itself acts like an enemy.

6.6.author: Swami Sivananda
6.6.text: The Self is the friend of the self of him by whom the Self has been conquered; but to the unconquered self, this Self stands in the position of an enemy, like an external foe.

6.6.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.6.text: To one who has conquered their lower nature with its help, the Self is a friend; but to one who has not done so, it is an enemy.

6.7.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.7.text: The thinking of the person, with a subdued mind and thus with complete calmness, remains in equilibrium in the case of others and himself, in cold and heat, in pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor.

6.7.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.7.text: Of him whose mind is conquered and who is serene, the great self is well-secured in heat and cold, in pleasure and pain, and in honor and dishonor.

6.7.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.7.text: The supreme Self of one who has control over the aggregate of his body and organs, and who is tranquil, becomes manifest. He should be poised in the midst of cold and heat, happiness and sorrow, as well as honor and dishonor.

6.7.author: Swami Sivananda
6.7.text: The Supreme Self of him who is self-controlled and peaceful remains balanced in cold and heat, pleasure and pain, as well as in honor and dishonor.

6.7.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.7.text: The Self of one who is self-controlled and has attained peace is equally unmoved by heat or cold, pleasure or pain, honor or dishonor.

6.8.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.8.text: He whose self is satisfied with knowledge and with what consists of varied thoughts; who remains peak-like and has completely subdued his senses; and to whom a clod, a stone, and a piece of gold are the same—that man of Yoga is called a master of Yoga.

6.8.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.8.text: The yogin whose mind is content with knowledge of the self and also with knowledge of the difference between the self and Prakrti, who is established in the self, whose senses are subdued, and to whom earth, stone, and gold all seem alike, is called integrated.

6.8.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.8.text: One whose mind is satisfied with knowledge and realization, who is unmoved, who has his organs under control, is said to be Self-absorbed. The yogi treats all alike, a lump of earth, a stone, and gold.

6.8.author: Swami Sivananda
6.8.text: The Yogi who is satisfied with the knowledge and wisdom of the Self, who has conquered the senses, and to whom a clod of earth, a piece of stone, and gold are all the same, is said to have attained Nirvikalpa Samadhi.

6.8.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.8.text: He who desires nothing but wisdom and spiritual insight, who has conquered his senses, and who looks upon a lump of earth, a stone, and fine gold with the same eye, is a real saint.

6.9.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.9.text: He whose mind is equal in the case of friend, companion, enemy, the indifferent one, the one who remains in the middle, the foe, the relative, the righteous, and also the sinful—he excels [all].

6.9.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.9.text: He who regards with an equal eye well-wishers, friends, foes, the indifferent, neutrals, the hateful, the relations, and even the good and the sinful—he excels.

6.9.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.9.text: He excels who has sameness of view with regard to a benefactor, a friend, an enemy, a neutral, an arbiter, the hateful, a relative, good people, and even sinners.

6.9.author: Swami Sivananda
6.9.text: He who is of the same mind towards the good-hearted, friends, enemies, the indifferent, the neutral, the hateful, the relatives, the righteous, and the unrighteous, excels.

6.9.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.9.text: He looks impartially on all—lovers, friends, or foes; indifferent, hostile, alien, or relative; virtuous or sinful.

6.10.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.10.text: Let the man of Yoga always yoke the self (mind) by remaining alone in a lonely place, controlling his mind and body, without desire and without a sense of possession.

6.10.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.10.text: The yogin should constantly fix his mind on yoga, remaining in a solitary place all alone, controlling his thoughts and mind, free from desire and a sense of possession.

6.10.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.10.text: A yogi should constantly concentrate his mind by staying in a solitary place, alone, with mind and body controlled, free from expectations, and free from acquisition.

6.10.author: Swami Sivananda
6.10.text: Let the yogi constantly strive to keep the mind steady, remaining in solitude, alone, with the body and mind controlled, and free from hope and greed.

6.10.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.10.text: Let the student of spirituality try unceasingly to concentrate his mind; let him live in seclusion, absolutely alone, with his mind and personality controlled, free from desire and without possessions.

6.11.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.11.text: Setting up in a clean place his own suitable, firm seat predominantly made of cloth, skin, and kusa-grass, neither too high nor too low for him;

6.11.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.11.text: Having established for himself, in a clean spot, a firm seat that is neither too high nor too low, and covering it with cloth, deer-skin, and Kusa grass in reverse order—

6.11.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.11.text: Having firmly established in a clean place his seat, neither too high nor too low, composed of cloth, skin, and kusa-grass placed successively one below the other;

6.11.author: Swami Sivananda
6.11.text: In a clean spot, having established a firm seat of his own, neither too high nor too low, made of cloth, skin, and kusha grass layered one over the other.

6.11.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.11.text: Having chosen a holy place, let him sit in a firm posture on a seat that is neither too high nor too low, and cover it with a grass mat, a deer skin, and a cloth.

6.12.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.12.text: Sitting there on the seat and making the mind single-pointed, let him, with the activities of his mind and senses subdued, practice Yoga for self-purification.

6.12.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.12.text: Sitting on the seat, with a concentrated mind, controlling the mind and senses, one should practice Yoga for the purification of the self.

6.12.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.12.text: Sitting on that seat, he should concentrate his mind for the purification of the internal organ, making the mind one-pointed and keeping the actions of the mind and senses under control.

6.12.author: Swami Sivananda
6.12.text: There, having made the mind one-pointed, with the actions of the mind and senses controlled, let him, seated on the seat, practice Yoga for the purification of the self.

6.12.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.12.text: Seated thus, with his mind concentrated, his functions controlled, and his senses governed, let him practice meditation for the purification of his lower nature.

6.13.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.13.text: Holding the body, head, and neck erect and motionless; remaining firm; looking properly at one's own nose-tip; and not looking in different directions.

6.13.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.13.text: Holding the trunk, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady, gazing at the tip of the nose and not looking in any direction;

6.13.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.13.text: Holding the body, head, and neck erect and still, being steady, looking at the tip of his own nose and not looking around.

6.13.author: Swami Sivananda
6.13.text: Let him firmly hold his body, head, and neck erect and still, gazing at the tip of his nose without looking around.

6.13.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.13.text: Let him hold his body, head, and neck erect, motionless and steady; let him look fixedly at the tip of his nose, turning neither to the right nor to the left.

6.14.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.14.text: Being calm-minded, fearless, and firmly devoted to celibacy; controlling the mind completely; let the master of Yoga remain, fixing his mind on Me and having Me as his supreme goal.

6.14.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.14.text: Serene and fearless, firm in their vow of celibacy, controlling their minds and fixing their thoughts on Me, they should sit in Yoga, intent on Me.

6.14.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.14.text: He should remain seated with a placid mind, free from fear, firm in the vow of celibacy, and with the mind fixed on Me by controlling it through concentration, having Me as the supreme goal.

6.14.author: Swami Sivananda
6.14.text: Serene-minded, fearless, firm in the vow of a Brahmachari, having controlled their mind, thinking of Me and balanced in mind, let them sit, having Me as their supreme goal.

6.14.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.14.text: With peace in his heart and no fear, observing the vow of celibacy, with his mind controlled and fixed on Me, let the student lose himself in contemplation of Me.

6.15.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.15.text: Yoking his mind incessantly in this manner, My devotee, with their mind not attached to anything else, realizes peace which culminates in nirvana and ends in Me.

6.15.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.15.text: Applying his mind in this way, the Yogin of controlled mind, ever attains the peace which is the summit of beatitude and which abides in Me.

6.15.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.15.text: Concentrating the mind thus, forever, the yogi of a controlled mind achieves the peace that culminates in liberation and abides in Me.

6.15.author: Swami Sivananda
6.15.text: Thus, always keeping the mind balanced, the yogi, with the mind controlled, attains the peace abiding in Me, culminating in liberation.

6.15.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.15.text: Thus, keeping his mind always in communion with Me and subduing his thoughts, he shall attain that Peace which is Mine and will lead him to liberation at last.

6.16.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.16.text: Yoga is neither for him who eats too much, nor for him who totally abstains from eating, nor for him who is prone to sleeping too much, nor for him who keeps awake too much.

6.16.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.16.text: Yoga is not for him who overeats, nor for him who fasts excessively; not for him, O Arjuna, who sleeps too much, nor for him who stays awake too long.

6.16.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.16.text: But, O Arjuna, Yoga is not for one who eats excessively, nor for one who does not eat at all; neither for one who habitually sleeps too long, nor for one who stays awake.

6.16.author: Swami Sivananda
6.16.text: Verily, Yoga is not possible for him who eats too much, nor for him who does not eat at all, nor for him who sleeps too much, nor for him who is always awake, O Arjuna.

6.16.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.16.text: Meditation is not for him who eats too much, nor for him who eats not at all; not for him who is overly addicted to sleep, nor for him who is always awake.

6.17.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.17.text: The Yoga becomes a misery-killer for him whose effort for food is appropriate, exertion in activities is proper, and whose sleep and waking are proportionate.

6.17.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.17.text: Yoga becomes the destroyer of sorrows for those who are temperate in food and recreation, temperate in their actions, and temperate in their sleep and wakefulness.

6.17.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.17.text: Yoga becomes a destroyer of sorrow for one whose eating and movements are regulated, whose effort in works is moderate, and whose sleep and wakefulness are temperate.

6.17.author: Swami Sivananda
6.17.text: Yoga becomes the destroyer of pain for him who is moderate in eating and recreation (such as walking, etc.), who exercises moderation in action, and who is moderate in sleep and wakefulness.

6.17.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.17.text: But for him who regulates his food and recreation, who is balanced in action, in sleep, and in waking, it shall dispel all unhappiness.

6.18.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.18.text: When his mind, well-controlled, is established in nothing but the Self, and he is free from craving for any desired object—at that time he is called a master of Yoga.

6.18.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.18.text: When the subdued mind rests solely on the Self, then, free from all yearning for objects of desire, one is said to be fit for Yoga.

6.18.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.18.text: A person who has become free from hankering for all desirable objects is said to be Self-absorbed when the controlled mind rests solely in the Self.

6.18.author: Swami Sivananda
6.18.text: When the perfectly controlled mind rests in the Self alone, free from longing for any of the objects of desire, then it is said, 'He is united'.

6.18.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.18.text: When the mind is completely controlled, centered in the Self, and free from all earthly desires, then the man is truly spiritual.

6.19.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.19.text: Just as a lamp in a windless place does not shake, this simile is recalled in the case of the man of Yoga, with a subdued mind, practicing Yoga in the Self.

6.19.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.19.text: "A lamp does not flicker in a windless place"—that is the simile used for the tranquil mind of a yogi who practices yoga.

6.19.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.19.text: As a lamp kept in a windless place does not flicker, so is the simile for the yogi whose mind is under control and who is engaged in concentration on the Self.

6.19.author: Swami Sivananda
6.19.text: As a lamp placed in a windless spot does not flicker, so is the Yogi of a controlled mind, who practices Yoga in the Self, compared.

6.19.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.19.text: The wise man who has conquered his mind and is absorbed in the Self is like a lamp that does not flicker, as it stands sheltered from every wind.

6.20.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.20.text: Where the mind, restrained through yoga practice, remains still; and where, observing, the yogi finds satisfaction in the Self alone, by perceiving only the Self within.

6.20.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.20.text: Where the mind, controlled through the practice of Yoga, rests, and where one sees the Self by the Self and is delighted by the Self alone.

6.20.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.20.text: At the time when the mind, restrained through the practice of Yoga, is withdrawn, and just when one sees the Self by the self and remains contented in the Self alone;

6.20.author: Swami Sivananda
6.20.text: When the mind, restrained by the practice of yoga, attains quietude, and when one sees the Self by the Self, they are satisfied in their own Self.

6.20.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.20.text: There, where the whole of nature is seen in the light of the Self, where the person abides within their Self and is satisfied there, their functions restrained by their union with the Divine, the mind finds rest.

6.21.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.21.text: Where he realizes the limitless Bliss, which is to be grasped by intellect and is beyond the senses; remaining where he does not depart from the Reality.

6.21.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.21.text: Where one knows that infinite happiness which can be grasped by the intellect but is beyond the reach of the senses, and is established in that condition, one does not swerve from it.

6.21.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.21.text: When one experiences that absolute Bliss, which can be intuited by the intellect and which is beyond the senses, and being thus established, this person surely does not swerve from Reality.

6.21.author: Swami Sivananda
6.21.text: When he (the Yogi) feels that infinite bliss which can be grasped by the pure intellect and which transcends the senses, and is established therein, never moving away from the reality.

6.21.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.21.text: When he enjoys the bliss that surpasses the senses and can only be grasped by the pure intellect, when he comes to rest within his highest self, he will never again stray from reality.

6.22.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.22.text: And having attained it, he does not think of any other gain as superior to that; being established in it, he is not shaken much by misery, however powerful it may be.

6.22.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.22.text: Having gained it, one holds that there is no greater gain; being established in it, one is not moved even by the heaviest sorrow.

6.22.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.22.text: Obtaining which one does not consider any other acquisition to be superior, and being established in which one is not perturbed even by great sorrow;

6.22.author: Swami Sivananda
6.22.text: Having obtained it, he thinks there is no other gain superior to it; established in it, he is not moved even by heavy sorrow.

6.22.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.22.text: Finding That, he will realize that there is no possession so precious. And once established there, no calamity can disturb him.

6.23.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.23.text: That he would realize to be the cause for his cessation of contact with misery and to be the one made known by Yoga. With determination, that is to be yoked in Yoga by a person of undepressed mind (or of the depressed mind).

6.23.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.23.text: Know this deliverance from association with misery to be Yoga. This Yoga must be practiced with determination and with a mind free from despondency.

6.23.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.23.text: One should know that severance of contact with sorrow to be what is called Yoga. That Yoga should be practiced with perseverance and with an undepressed heart.

6.23.author: Swami Sivananda
6.23.text: Let this be known by the name of Yoga, the severance from union with pain. This Yoga should be practiced with determination and with an undespairing mind.

6.23.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.23.text: This inner severance from the affliction of misery is spirituality. It should be practiced with determination and with a heart that refuses to be depressed.

6.24.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.24.text: In order to renounce completely all desires that are born of intention, let a person restrain the group of sense-organs from all sides by mind alone.

6.24.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.24.text: Renouncing entirely all desires born of volition and restraining the mind from all the senses on all sides,

6.24.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.24.text: By totally eschewing all desires that arise from thoughts and restraining all the organs with the mind from every side;

6.24.author: Swami Sivananda
6.24.text: Abandoning unreservedly all desires born of Sankalpa (thought and imagination) and completely restraining the whole group of senses by the mind from all sides.

6.24.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.24.text: Renouncing every desire that can be imagined, controlling the senses at every point through the power of the mind;

6.25.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.25.text: Very slowly remain still, keeping the mind well established in the Self by means of the intellect held in steadiness; and let him not think of anything (object).

6.25.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.25.text: Little by little, one should withdraw oneself from objects other than the self, with the help of the intellect held by firm resolution; and then one should think of nothing else, having fixed the mind upon the Self.

6.25.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.25.text: One should gradually withdraw with the intellect, endowed with steadiness. Making the mind fixed in the Self, one should not think of anything at all.

6.25.author: Swami Sivananda
6.25.text: Little by little, let him attain steadiness of the intellect by holding it firmly; having made the mind establish itself in the Self, let him not think of anything else.

6.25.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.25.text: Little by little, with the help of his reason controlled by fortitude, let him attain peace; and, fixing his mind on the Self, let him not think of anything else.

6.26.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.26.text: By whatever things the shaky and unsteady mind strays, let him restrain it from those things and bring it back under the control of the Self alone.

6.26.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.26.text: Wherever the fickle and unsteady mind wanders, one should subdue it and then bring it back under the control of the self alone.

6.26.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.26.text: The yogi should bring this mind under the subjugation of the Self itself, restraining it from all those causes that cause the restless, unsteady mind to wander away.

6.26.author: Swami Sivananda
6.26.text: From whatever cause the restless and unsteady mind wanders away, let him restrain it from that and bring it under the control of the Self alone.

6.26.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.26.text: When the volatile and wavering mind wanders, let him restrain it and bring it back to its allegiance to the Self.

6.27.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.27.text: Indeed, the Supreme Bliss comes to this highly tranquil-minded man of Yoga, whose passions remain stilled, who has become one with the Brahman, and who is free from sins.

6.27.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.27.text: For supreme happiness comes to the Yogin whose mind is at peace, who is free from evil, from whom Rajas has departed, and who has become the Brahman.

6.27.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.27.text: Supreme Bliss comes to this yogi alone whose mind has become perfectly tranquil, whose quality of rajas has been eliminated, who has become identified with Brahman, and is untainted.

6.27.author: Swami Sivananda
6.27.text: Supreme Bliss indeed comes to this Yogi whose mind is made peaceful, whose passion is quelled, who has become Brahman, and who is free from sin.

6.27.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.27.text: Supreme bliss is the lot of the sage whose mind attains peace, whose passions subside, who is without sin, and who becomes one with the Absolute.

6.28.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.28.text: Thus, yoking the self always, the man of Yoga, with a subdued mind, easily attains complete union, that is, the Brahman.

6.28.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.28.text: Thus, devoting himself to the Yoga of the Self, freed from impurities, the yogin easily attains the supreme bliss of contact with the Brahman.

6.28.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.28.text: By constantly concentrating his mind in this way, the taintless yogi easily attains the absolute bliss of contact with Brahman.

6.28.author: Swami Sivananda
6.28.text: The yogi, always engaging the mind thus (in the practice of yoga), is freed from sins and easily enjoys the infinite bliss of contact with Brahman (the Eternal).

6.28.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.28.text: Thus, free from sin, abiding always in the Eternal, the saint enjoys, without effort, the bliss that flows from the realization of the Infinite.

6.29.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.29.text: He who has yoked himself in Yoga and observes everything truly perceives the Self to be abiding in all beings and all beings to be abiding in the Self.

6.29.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.29.text: He whose mind is fixed in Yoga sees reality everywhere; he sees his Self as abiding in all beings and all beings in his Self.

6.29.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.29.text: One who has their mind Self-absorbed through Yoga, and who has the vision of sameness everywhere, sees this Self existing in everything, and everything in their Self.

6.29.author: Swami Sivananda
6.29.text: With the mind harmonized by Yoga, he sees the Self abiding in all beings and all beings in the Self; he sees the same everywhere.

6.29.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.29.text: He who experiences the unity of life sees his own Self in all beings, and all beings in his own Self, and looks upon everything with an impartial eye.

6.30.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.30.text: He who observes Me in all and observes all in Me—for him, I am not lost, and he too is not lost for me.

6.30.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.30.text: To him who sees Me in every self and every self in Me—I am not lost to him, nor is he lost to Me.

6.30.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.30.text: One who sees Me in everything and sees all things in Me—I do not lose sight of him, and he also is not lost to My vision.

6.30.author: Swami Sivananda
6.30.text: He who sees Me everywhere and sees everything in Me, never becomes separated from Me, nor do I from him.

6.30.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.30.text: He who sees Me in everything and everything in Me, I shall never forsake him, nor shall he lose Me.

6.31.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.31.text: He who is firmly established in the oneness of Me, experiences Me immanent in all beings—that man of Yoga is never stained, no matter what stage he may be in.

6.31.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.31.text: The yogi who, fixed in oneness, worships Me dwelling in all beings—he abides in Me, no matter how he may live.

6.31.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.31.text: That yogi, who, being established in unity, adores Me as existing in all things, exists in Me—in whatever condition he may be.

6.31.author: Swami Sivananda
6.31.text: He who, being established in unity, worships Me, who dwells in all beings, that yogi abides in Me, whatever their mode of living may be.

6.31.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.31.text: The sage who realizes the unity of life and who worships Me in all beings, lives in Me, no matter what their lot may be.

6.32.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.32.text: Whoever finds pleasure or pain equally in all, as if it were in themselves—that person is considered to be a great man of Yoga, O Arjuna!

6.32.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.32.text: He who, due to the similarity of selves everywhere, sees pleasure or pain as the same everywhere—that yogi, O Arjuna, is considered the closest.

6.32.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.32.text: O Arjuna, that yogi is considered the best who judges what is happiness and sorrow in all beings by the same standard as they would apply to themselves.

6.32.author: Swami Sivananda
6.32.text: He who, through the likeness of the Self, O Arjuna, sees reality everywhere, be it pleasure or pain, is regarded as the highest Yogi.

6.32.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.32.text: O Arjuna! He is the perfect saint who, having been taught by the likeness within himself, sees the same Self everywhere, regardless of whether the outer form be pleasurable or painful.

6.33.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.33.text: Arjuna said, "O slayer of Mandhu, this Yoga of equanimity which You have spoken of, I do not find a proper foundation for it due to the unsteadiness of the mind."

6.33.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.33.text: Arjuna said, "O Krsna, this Yoga of reality, which You have declared, I do not see how it can be steady due to the fickleness of the mind."

6.33.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.33.text: Arjuna said, "O Madhusudana (Krsna), this Yoga that You have spoken of as sameness, I do not see its steady continuance due to the restlessness of the mind."

6.33.author: Swami Sivananda
6.33.text: Arjuna said, "O Krishna, I do not see how this Yoga of equanimity, which you have taught me, can be maintained steadily, due to the restlessness of the mind."

6.33.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.33.text: Arjuna said: I do not see how I can attain this state of equanimity which You have revealed, owing to the restlessness of my mind.

6.34.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.34.text: O Krsna! The mind is indeed unsteady, destructive, strong, and obstinate; I believe it is very difficult to control it, just as it is to control the wind.

6.34.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.34.text: For the mind is fickle, O Krsna, impetuous, powerful, and stubborn; I think that restraining it is as difficult as restraining the wind.

6.34.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.34.text: For, O Kṛṣṇa, the mind is unsteady, turbulent, strong, and obstinate; I consider its control to be as difficult as that of the wind.

6.34.author: Swami Sivananda
6.34.text: The mind is indeed restless, turbulent, strong, and unyielding, O Krishna; I consider it as difficult to control as controlling the wind.

6.34.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.34.text: My Lord! Verily, the mind is fickle and turbulent, obstinate, and strong; indeed, it is extremely difficult to control, like the wind.

6.35.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.35.text: The Bhagavat said, O mighty-armed one! No doubt, the mind is unsteady and hard to control. But it can be controlled through practice and an attitude of desirelessness, O son of Kunti!

6.35.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.35.text: The Lord said, "The mind is indeed hard to subdue and fickle, O mighty-armed one, but, O son of Kunti, it can be brought under control through practice and the exercise of dispassion."

6.35.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.35.text: The Blessed Lord said, O mighty-armed one, undoubtedly the mind is untamable and restless. But, O son of Kunti, it can be brought under control through practice and detachment.

6.35.author: Swami Sivananda
6.35.text: The Blessed Lord said, "Undoubtedly, O mighty-armed Arjuna, the mind is difficult to control and restless; but with practice and dispassion, it can be restrained."

6.35.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.35.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: Doubtless, O Mighty One, the mind is fickle and exceedingly difficult to restrain; however, O Son of Kunti, with practice and renunciation, it can be done.

6.36.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.36.text: My belief is that attaining Yoga is difficult for a person with an uncontrolled mind; but it is possible to attain by proper means with a subdued self.

6.36.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.36.text: In my opinion, Yoga is hard to attain by a person of an unrestrained mind; however, it can be attained through the right means by one who strives for it and has a subdued mind.

6.36.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.36.text: My conviction is that Yoga is difficult to attain for one with an uncontrolled mind. But it is possible to attain through the aforementioned means for one who strives and has a controlled mind.

6.36.author: Swami Sivananda
6.36.text: I think Yoga is hard to be attained by one with an uncontrolled self, but the self-controlled and striving one can attain it by the appropriate means.

6.36.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.36.text: It is not possible to attain Self-Realization unless one knows how to control oneself; however, for one who, striving by the proper means, learns such control, it is possible.

6.37.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.37.text: Arjuna said, "A person who has faith and is desirous of reaching the path of the good, but whose mind has been severed from Yoga—to which goal does he go, having failed to attain success in Yoga? O Krsna!"

6.37.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.37.text: Arjuna said, "If a person who is possessed of faith but has put in only inadequate effort finds his mind wandering away from Yoga, and then fails to attain perfection—what way does he go, O Krishna?"

6.37.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.37.text: Arjuna said, "O Krsna, what goal does one attain who, despite having faith, fails to achieve perfection in Yoga due to lack of diligence, and whose mind becomes deflected from Yoga?"

6.37.author: Swami Sivananda
6.37.text: Arjuna said, "He who is unable to control himself, even though he has faith, and whose mind wanders away from Yoga, what end does he meet, having failed to attain perfection in Yoga, O Krishna?"

6.37.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.37.text: Arjuna asked: What of him who fails to control himself, whose mind falls from spiritual contemplation, yet retains his faith and does not attain perfection?

6.38.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.38.text: Does he, fallen from both, get lost like a broken cloud? Or, O mighty-armed one! Having no support, does he meet total destruction?

6.38.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.38.text: Without any support, confused in the path leading to the Brahman, and thus having fallen from both, does he not perish, O mighty-armed one, like a rent cloud?

6.38.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.38.text: O Mighty-armed one, having fallen from both [paths], without support, deluded on the path to Brahman, does he not get ruined like a scattered cloud?

6.38.author: Swami Sivananda
6.38.text: Fallen from both, does he not perish like a rent cloud, supportless, O mighty-armed one, deluded on the path of Brahman?

6.38.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.38.text: Having failed in both, my Lord, is he without hope, like a riven cloud with no support, lost on the spiritual path?

6.39.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.39.text: Please dispel this doubt of mine completely. But for You, O Krsna, no one else is capable of eradicating this doubt.

6.39.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.39.text: O Krsna, you should altogether remove this doubt of mine, for there is no other remover of this doubt than you.

6.39.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.39.text: O Krsna, you should totally eradicate this doubt of mine, for none other than yourself can be the dispeller of this doubt!

6.39.author: Swami Sivananda
6.39.text: O Krishna, please completely dispel this doubt of mine, for it is not possible for anyone but You to do so.

6.39.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.39.text: My Lord! You are worthy to solve this doubt once and for all; there is no one else competent to do so, save Yourself.

6.40.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.40.text: The Bhagavat said, "O dear Partha! Neither in this world nor in the other is there destruction for him. Certainly, no one who performs an auspicious act ever comes to a grievous state."

6.40.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.40.text: The Lord said, "Neither here in this world nor there in the next is there destruction for him. For no one who does good ever comes to an evil end."

6.40.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.40.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O Partha, there is certainly no ruin for him here or hereafter, for no one engaged in good meets with a deplorable end, my son!"

6.40.author: Swami Sivananda
6.40.text: The Blessed Lord said, "O Arjuna, neither in this world nor in the next will there be destruction for him; none, indeed, who does good, O my son, ever comes to grief."

6.40.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.40.text: Lord Shri Krishna replied: My beloved child! There is no destruction for him, either in this world or the next. No evil fate awaits him who treads the path of righteousness.

6.41.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.41.text: Having attained the worlds of those who perform pious acts, and having resided there for years of eternity, the one who has fallen from Yoga is born again in the house of the pure and wealthy.

6.41.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.41.text: He who has fallen away from Yoga is born again in the house of the pure and prosperous, having attained to the worlds of doers of good deeds and dwelled there for many long years.

6.41.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.41.text: Attaining the worlds of the righteous and residing there for eternal years, the man who has fallen from Yoga is born in the house of the pious and prosperous.

6.41.author: Swami Sivananda
6.41.text: Having attained to the worlds of the righteous and having dwelt there for everlasting years, he who fell from Yoga is born in a house of the pure and wealthy.

6.41.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.41.text: Having reached the worlds where the righteous dwell, and having remained there for many years, he who has strayed from the path of spirituality will be born again into the family of the pure, benevolent, and prosperous.

6.42.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.42.text: Or, he is born nowhere else but in the family of the intelligent men of Yoga; for, this birth is more difficult to obtain in the world.

6.42.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.42.text: Or he is born into a family of wise yogis. But such a birth in this world is rare.

6.42.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.42.text: Or, he is born in the family of wise yogis. Such a birth is indeed more difficult to come by in the world.

6.42.author: Swami Sivananda
6.42.text: Or he is born in a family of even the wisest of yogis; verily, such a birth is very difficult to obtain in this world.

6.42.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.42.text: Or, he may be born in the family of wise sages, though such a birth is indeed very difficult to obtain.

6.43.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.43.text: There, in that life, he regains the link of mentality transmitted from his former body. Consequently, once again he strives for full success, O rejoicer of the Kurus!

6.43.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.43.text: There, O Arjuna, he regains the disposition of mind that he had in his former body, and from there he strives even more for success in Yoga.

6.43.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.43.text: There he becomes endowed with the wisdom acquired in the previous body, and he strives even more than before for perfection, O scion of the Kuru dynasty.

6.43.author: Swami Sivananda
6.43.text: Then he comes into contact with the knowledge acquired in his former body and strives even more for perfection, O Arjuna.

6.43.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.43.text: Then, the experience acquired in his former life will revive, and with it, he will more eagerly strive for perfection than before.

6.44.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.44.text: Not being a master of himself, he is only dragged by that former practice (its mental impression); only a seeker of the knowledge of Yoga passes beyond what strengthens the [sacred] text.

6.44.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.44.text: By the power of his earlier practice, he is carried forward even against his will. Even though he is an enquirer about Yoga, he transcends the Sabda-Brahman, i.e., Prakṛti or matter.

6.44.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.44.text: For, by that very past practice, he is carried forward even in spite of himself! Even a seeker of Yoga transcends the results of the performance of Vedic rituals!

6.44.author: Swami Sivananda
6.44.text: By that same former practice, he is borne on in spite of himself. Even he who merely wishes to know Yoga goes beyond the Brahmanic word.

6.44.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.44.text: Unconsciously, he will return to the practices of his old life; thus, one who strives to attain spiritual consciousness is certainly superior to one who merely talks about it.

6.45.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.45.text: After that, the assiduous man of Yoga, having his sins completely cleansed and being perfected through many births, reaches the Supreme Goal.

6.45.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.45.text: But the yogi, striving earnestly, cleansed of all his stains and perfected through many births, reaches the supreme state.

6.45.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.45.text: However, the yogi, applying himself assiduously, becoming purified from sin and attaining perfection through many births, they achieve the highest Goal.

6.45.author: Swami Sivananda
6.45.text: But the Yogi who strives assiduously, purified of sins and perfected gradually over many births, reaches the highest goal.

6.45.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.45.text: Then, after many lives of earnest striving and absolution of sins, the student of spirituality attains perfection and reaches the Supreme.

6.46.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.46.text: The person of Yoga is superior to the persons of austerities and is considered superior even to the persons of knowledge; and the person of Yoga is superior to the persons of action. Therefore, O Arjuna! you should become a person of Yoga.

6.46.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.46.text: Greater than the ascetics, greater than those who possess knowledge, greater than the ritualists is the Yogin. Therefore, O Arjuna, become a Yogin.

6.46.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.46.text: A yogi is higher than those of austerity; they are considered higher even than those of knowledge. The yogi is also higher than those of action. Therefore, O Arjuna, become a yogi.

6.46.author: Swami Sivananda
6.46.text: The yogi is thought to be superior to the ascetics, even superior to those who have knowledge obtained through the study of scriptures; he is also superior to men of action; therefore, be thou a yogi, O Arjuna.

6.46.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.46.text: The wise person is superior to the ascetic, the scholar, and the man of action; therefore, be thou a wise person, O Arjuna!

6.47.author: Dr. S. Sankaranarayan
6.47.text: He who has faith and serves Me with his inner self devoted to Me, is considered by Me to be the best of all yogis.

6.47.author: Swami Adidevananda
6.47.text: He who, with faith, worships Me, and whose innermost self is fixed in Me, I consider him to be the greatest of the Yogins.

6.47.author: Swami Gambirananda
6.47.text: Even among all the yogis, he who adores Me with his mind fixed on Me and with faith is considered by Me to be the best of the yogis.

6.47.author: Swami Sivananda
6.47.text: And among all the Yogis, he who, full of faith and with his inner self merged in Me, worships Me is deemed by Me to be the most devoted.

6.47.author: Shri Purohit Swami
6.47.text: I look upon him as the best of mystics, who, full of faith, worships Me and abides in Me.
